{{nihongo|'''Kawara Shrine'''|川原神社|かわらじんじゃ}} is an {{ill|lt=sessha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|1=Setsumatsusha}} (auxiliary shrine) of {{ill|lt=Kōtai Jingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011|1=Kōtai Jingū}} (Inner Shrine) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Grand Shrine|qid=Q687168|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}, listed in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]] and located in [[Ise Province]].
== Overview ==
It ranks 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>
It is a {{ill|lt=shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} designated by {{ill|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, and the {{ill|lt=enshrined deity|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100|1=Saijin}} is said to be the {{ill|lt=guardian deity|Q131278957|qid=Q131278957|1=Guardian deities}} of the {{ill|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|Q6884164|qid=Q6884164|1=Miya River (Mie)}}.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 71</ref>
The shrine is located on the east bank of the Miyagawa River,<ref name="gk"/> at 1559 Sensui, aza Sōchi, Sōchi-chō, {{ill|lt=Ise City|Q328067|qid=Q328067|1=Ise, Mie}}, {{ill|lt=Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196|1=Mie Prefecture}}.<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 76</ref> The place name "Sōchi" means "marshland," indicating that wetlands from the Miyagawa once existed there.<ref name="gk"/> There are also records stating that rice was offered from Sōchi to the Inner Shrine.<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 346</ref>
The shrine name appears as "Kawara Shrine" in the ''Kōtaijingū Gishikichō'', while other sources list it as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha." Records state that local residents referred to it as "Senzui" (river water, spring water), "Odago," or "Yagura."<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 345</ref>
== Precincts ==
The shrine grounds cover an {{ill|lt=area|Q11500|qid=Q11500|1=Area}} of 3,219 {{ill|lt=square meters|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m<sup>2</sup>|1=Square metre}}.<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 347</ref> The {{ill|lt=precincts|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002|1=keidai}} form a tranquil space filled with dappled sunlight, birdsong, and the murmur of the river.<ref name="ic"/> Trees such as {{ill|lt=Japanese cypress|Q917187|qid=Q917187|1=Chamaecyparis obtusa}}, {{ill|lt=camphor tree|Q158722|qid=Q158722|1=Camphora officinarum}}, {{ill|lt=oak|Q796117|qid=Q796117|1=Cyclobalanopsis}}, {{ill|lt=Machilus thunbergii|Q5792073|qid=Q5792073|1=Machilus thunbergii}}, and {{ill|lt=Ilex latifolia|Q2706373|qid=Q2706373|1=Ilex latifolia}} grow densely within the grounds.<ref name="sk7"/>
== Enshrined deity ==
The enshrined deity is {{ill|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}.<ref name="ic"/> This is the same {{ill|lt=deity (Shinto)|Q524158|qid=Q524158|lt=kami|1=Kami}} worshipped at the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya|1=UNKNOWN}} and {{ill|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Yoru-no-miya)|Q11516023|qid=Q11516023|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)}}, among the 125 shrines of Ise Grand Shrine.<ref name="tm"/> While Tsukuyomi is generally regarded as a {{ill|lt=moon|Q405|qid=Q405|1=Moon}} deity, the moon and {{ill|lt=water|Q283|qid=Q283|1=Water}} are considered closely related, and in the context of Kawara Shrine, Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama is regarded as a river deity.<ref name="ic"/>
In addition to sharing the same enshrined deity, there is a theory that Sōchi-chō, where Kawara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-chō, where Tsukiyomi Shrine is located, were both deeply connected through the {{ill|lt=Arakida clan|Q11618716|qid=Q11618716|1=Arakida clan}}.<ref name="sk6"/>
== History ==
According to tradition, {{ill|lt=Yamatohime-no-Mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732|1=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was welcomed here by Ōwakako-no-Mikoto and traveled down the Miyagawa River by boat.<ref name="ic"/> Regarding its establishment, based on the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, it is believed to have been founded before the compilation of the ''{{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}'', that is, before the 5th year of {{ill|lt=Enchō (era)|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō|1=Enchō}} ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|qid=Q30470|1=927}}).<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 22</ref> According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was designated as one of the shrines involved in repairs by the {{ill|lt=chief priest|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|1=Gūji}}, and it received offerings during the Kinensai and Kannamesai festivals.<ref name="sk5"/> However, during the {{ill|lt=Sengoku period (Japan)|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period|1=Sengoku period}}, {{ill|lt=rituals|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824|1=Saitan-sai}} were discontinued,<ref name="tm"/> and the shrine grounds fell into ruin.<ref name="sk5"/> The hereditary priests ({{ill|lt=hafuri|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|lt=hafuri|1=Gūji}}) who had been appointed until then also died out.<ref name="sk6"/>
In the 3rd year of {{ill|lt=Kanbun|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228|1=Kanbun (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577|1=1663}}), {{ill|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga|Q92924151|qid=Q92924151|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga|1=Kiyonaga Kawabe}} restored the shrine at Sōchi.<ref name="sk5"/> On the 9th day of the 9th month (lunar calendar; {{ill|lt=Gregorian calendar|Q12138|qid=Q12138|1=Gregorian calendar}}: {{ill|lt=October 9|Q2923|qid=Q2923|1=October 9}}, 1663), the {{ill|lt=shrine buildings|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|1=Gūji}} were constructed, and on the 12th day of the 12th month (lunar calendar; Gregorian: {{ill|lt=January 10|Q2243|qid=Q2243|1=January 10}}, {{ill|lt=1664|Q7581|qid=Q7581|1=1664}}), the deity was ceremonially transferred ({{ill|lt=sengu|Q24892914|qid=Q24892914|1=Sengyo}}).<ref name="sk5"/> At that time, families that had formerly served as hereditary priests were sought out and reinstated.<ref name="sk6"/> During the restoration, local traditions and place names were referenced, but there is also a theory that Takehana Shrine in present-day Takegahana-chō, Ise City, or {{ill|lt=Kawarabuchi Shrine|Q17209232|qid=Q17209232|1=Kawarabuchi Shrine}} in {{ill|lt=Fun'e (Ise City)|Q17213313|qid=Q17213313|1=Funae}} may have been the original site.<ref name="tm"/> Since a subsequent deity transfer on the 29th day of the 3rd month of the 7th year of {{ill|lt=Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001|1=Genroku}} (lunar calendar; Gregorian: {{ill|lt=April 23|Q2527|qid=Q2527|1=April 23}}, {{ill|lt=1694|Q7694|qid=Q7694|1=1694}}), the shrine site has not moved.<ref name="sk5"/>
The shrine buildings were rebuilt in November {{ill|lt=1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056|1=1908}} ({{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 41).<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): p. 11</ref> They were subsequently rebuilt again in May {{ill|lt=1960|Q3754|qid=Q3754|1=1960}} ({{ill|lt=Shōwa|Q327567|qid=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}} 35), and repairs were carried out in September {{ill|lt=1983|Q2434|qid=Q2434|1=1983}} (Shōwa 58).<ref name="sk6"/>
== Rituals ==
During the Kinensai, {{ill|lt=Tsukinamisai|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri}} (June and December), {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|qid=Q11255045|1=Kannamesai Festival}}, {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}, and extraordinary festivals, {{ill|lt=Shinto priests|Q60523|qid=Q60523|1=Kannushi}} present {{ill|lt=offerings|Q11591045|qid=Q11591045|lt=shinsen|1=Shinsen}} and {{ill|lt=heihaku|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885|1=Hanpei}} before the shrine. For rites such as the {{ill|lt=Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824|1=Saitan-sai}}, remote worship is performed at the Inner Shrine's Gojōden Hall.<ref name="sk6"/>
== Access ==
The shrine is situated in a forest slightly off {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 22 (Ise–Minamishima Line)|Q11357908|qid=Q11357908|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 22}}.<ref>Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): pp. 346–347</ref>
* About a 12-minute walk (700 {{ill|lt=meters|Q11573|qid=Q11573|lt=m|1=Metre}}) from the "Sōchi" {{ill|lt=bus stop|Q953806|qid=Q953806|1=Bus stop}} on a {{ill|lt=Mie Kōtsū|Q6843516|qid=Q6843516|1=Mie Kotsu}} {{ill|lt=route bus|Q1373492|qid=Q1373492|1=Transit bus}}.<ref name="ic"/> Enter the alley opposite {{ill|lt=Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School|Q11379036|qid=Q11379036|1=Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School}} near the bus stop and follow the rice paddies to reach the precincts.<ref name="ic"/>
* Approximately 5.5 {{ill|lt=kilometers|Q828224|qid=Q828224|lt=km|1=Kilometre}} from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|qid=Q6079748|1=Iseshi Station}} on the {{ill|lt=JR Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023|1=Sangū Line}} of {{ill|lt=Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679|1=Central Japan Railway Company}} or the {{ill|lt=Kintetsu Yamada Line|Q900630|qid=Q900630|1=Yamada Line (Kintetsu)}} of {{ill|lt=Kintetsu|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085|1=Kintetsu Railway}}.<ref name="sk5"/>
